# dsh-control
English | 中文
**Every machine already runs dsh. Make this one window the front end for all of them.**

Chat with the dsh instances on your other machines, natively from your local sidebar.
Remote session

s stream back token by token; the remote uses its own model credentials,
tools and sandbox. Zero cha
nges on the remote. Zero dependencies. One-line install.

*Two dsh windows answering the same question. The left window shows a session auto-named
`控制端·<local

title>` (①) — that naming only happens on the machine the plugin drives. The right
window shows the

workspace `cn-dsh2` the plugin created (②) and the model route set to the
environment name (③).*
> 🎬 A 15-second capture (one-click connect → streaming reply) is being recorded.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Use the profile you already run (usually `web` or `desktop`). No build step, no native
modules, no d
ependencies — the plugin is plain JavaScript and installs as-is.
GitHub slow or blocked? Install from the release tarball instead

Download dsh-control-0.2.1.tgz
and run:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

After installing, **fully quit and reopen dsh** (⌘Q — closing the window is not enough),
then:

- Right sidebar →「远程 dsh 环境」→ type `user@host` → connect
- Left sidebar →「🌐 远程环境」→ pick the environm
ent tab to enter the remote's full UI
> Upgrades need the same ⌘Q: a plugin's host half loads at process start.

> An npm package (`dsh-control`) is prepared and can be published later; the GitHub
> command above
is the current install path.
## Install failed?

- **Retry once** — the install pulls the repo from GitHub and resolves peers from npm;
on a bad netw

ork pnpm can time out.
- **Seeing `allowBuilds` / "prepare script"** — that is dsh's generic hint fo

r *any*
failed git-hosted install. This plugin has no build scripts (its only script is
`test`), so

nothing needs approving; just retry.
- Still stuck? Use the release tarball instead (above).
## Versions & updating

- **What you get**: `github:6mt/dsh-control` installs the newest commit of `main` and
**pins it in y

our profile's lockfile** — it does not silently follow later commits.
- **Update**: `dsh plugin --pr

ofile <your profile> update dsh-control`, then ⌘Q
- **If it says "Already up to date" and the versio

n does not move** (you installed a
pinned `#vX.Y.Z` earlier), re-add the un-pinned form — verified t

(you installed a
pinned `#vX.Y.Z` earlier), re-add the un-pinned form — verified to pull the latest:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

- **Pin a version**: `github:6mt/dsh-control#v0.2.1` (tag) or `github:6mt/dsh-control#<commit>`
- Ch
anges are recorded in CHANGELOG.md.
## How is this different from the same-named `dsh-control` skill?

There is another project called `jacjackai/dsh-control` — a **skill** that lets an AI agent
operate

the DSH **on your own machine**. This repository is a **plugin** for a different
job: **across machi

nes**. It brings the dsh instances you already run on other servers into
one local window (their ses

sions appear natively in the sidebar, and the whole remote UI
can be opened in place). The two can c

ppear natively in the sidebar, and the whole remote UI
can be opened in place). The two can coexist.
## How is this different from dsh-remote / dsh-remote-ssh?
| | Remote-workspace plugins (dsh-remote, …) | **dsh-control** |
| The remote machine is a | **file system** (SFTP tool set) | **dsh that is already running there**

|
| Sessions live | local session + remote directory | **remote sessions, native in your sidebar** |
| Credentials & tools | configured locally, SSH config duplicated | the remote's own — nothing copi

ed |
| Remote needs | only SSH | dsh installed (≥0.2.0-rc.2) with its web instance running |
| Chang
es on the remote | some deploy dsh for you | **zero** (read-only probing + the remote's own API) |

The two **coexist** (tested side by side): no dsh on the remote → use dsh-remote;
dsh already there

* (tested side by side): no dsh on the remote → use dsh-remote;
dsh already there → use dsh-control.
## What it does

*The「远程 dsh 环境」panel: type `user@host` and connect — the row then reports its state and
whether the
environment already has its workspace.*

- **One-click connect** — type `user@host`; the plugin probes the remote dsh, fetches
its access tok

en and opens an encrypted channel (~5 s)
- **Automatic workspace** — each environment gets a same-na

med local workspace; any
session created inside it automatically becomes a remote session
- **True s

treaming** — remote replies flow in token by token, not dumped at the end
- **Paired naming** — remo

te sessions are named `控制端·<local title>`, so both sides match
- **Visible & self-healing** — remote

sessions are marked in the sidebar; disconnects
are reported honestly and repaired by one click
## Security

**What it does on your machine**: one state file
(`$DSH_HOME/dsh-control/state.json`, mode 0600, hol

ds the remote access tokens) and an
on-demand SSH tunnel process.
**What it never does**: no install

s or writes on the remote, no lifecycle management of
the remote dsh, never reads your other local c

redentials, tokens never enter logs.
When passwordless SSH is not set up it shows the exact one-line

fix — passwords are
never stored. Details in SECURITY.md.
## Known limitations

- The remote must already run dsh (≥ 0.2.0-rc.2) with its web instance (otherwise use a
remote-works

pace plugin)
- Connects over SSH (passwordless or configured key; a no-SSH "direct address" mode is

implemented but not yet exposed in the UI)
- The remote-environment page **is** the remote's own UI:

actions there really affect the
remote machine (exactly as if you opened it in a browser)
- The def

ault environment preloads in the background right after dsh boots (loaded
off-screen), so opening th

e page is instant; only the first seconds of a cold boot
still depend on the network
- Sidebar marke

rs and the streaming feel are verified by eye per release
- Cancelling a remote turn is implemented
but marked experimental
